City Powerless

By: Johann Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
If you are living in jozi, chances are that you are being billed a lot more for your electricity than you are actually using

Summary:
Ten years after they first admitted that they had billing problems, City Power recently went on record to say that it has been solved. But this is a lie - according to various legal firms, the Star Consumer Watch, and thousands of consumers. Wrong meter numbers, meters that are only ever estimated and never actually read and adjusted, and impossible consumption figures have lead to a chaos that is not about to be solved soon - and which is costing consumers millions of rands, and which leads to power and (illegal) water cuts by the council. Council has an approach of first pay the amount showing on your bill and then we will investigate your claim that it's wrong. This leads to the start of corruption from honest citizens - people who come to disconnect are simply bribed not to cut the power or water. At the same time this has also lead to various scams appearing - people who either work for city power or act as if they do, arrive at your gate and threaten to disconnect you unless you pay a bribe. We even have a case study of a guy who was phoned by someone from city power and told that they were mailing him his account and he had to pay R35 000 to bring it up to date - he received the account via email, paid the money and then realised a few days later that he was scammed. He went to City Power, phoned the guy's number from another official's desk, and they heard the phone ring in an empty cubicle down the passage.
According to one lawyer we interviewed, the matter should really be taken to concourt - as an old bylaw seems to lie at the heart of the problem - this states that the burden of proof in cases against the municipality lies with the consumer - meaning that we all have to do our own daily readings with photographs. In spite of this, they have a whole dapertment dealing with these cases only, and in 8 years have only lost three cases.

Press Release:


City Powerless
After ten years of billing chaos, the City of Joburg claims that, thanks to its Smart Meter rollout, incorrect accounts are a thing of the past. Not so, say furious residents who continue to battle exorbitant water and electricity bills to no avail. To add to the problem, criminals pretending to be City Power disconnection teams are cashing in on the crisis. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


For a few dollars more...



Studio intro
About ten years ago residents in Johannesburg started having massive problems with their monthly water and lights accounts. The municipality changed the billing system and this caused endless problems. In 2013 they announced that they were rolling out smart meters to sort out the crisis. And in the beginning of 2016 they announced that the billing crisis was something of the past. But is this true?




Opening scene: re-enactment

It normally happens at the most inconvenient time – two people arrive at your gate and say that they are subcontractors working for city power and they've come to disconnect you because your account is in arrears.
You panic, because you can't afford to be without lights or water. And then....you give the gentlemen a little something, a few hundred rand or a bottle of whisky, and they go away until next month...
External shot City Power
Yumna Sheik from City Power says this behaviour is unacceptable
Yumna Shaik, Spokesperson City Power
We will not condone bribery on the part of our contractors, but we do not condone bribery on the part of our customers as well. A customer should not be bribing an employee of the city.
Generic shots of Joburg.
Interior shots of Client Customer Centre
But what if the bribers are normally law abiding citisens who have just become desperate victims of a non-functioning system? The billing crisis has now been with us for a decade, and back when it started it was blamed on incompetent meter readers, extended periods of estimated readings in stead of actual readings and new billing software. This was one of the main reasons why they spent R1.2billion to roll out the smart meters – these would send actual readings via sim card directly to the billing department, eliminating both meter readers and estimated readings. To date they've rolled out more than 100 000 smart meters, but in spite of the municipality's announcement in january that the problems are a thing of the past, they're still getting an average of 15000 complaints per month.
Bongani link in front of City of Joburg
Thuso House – The house of help. This is where you are supposed to come to get your City of Joburg billing problems resolved. But many complainants say this isn't what happened and they've lost faith.
Annette Lawrence entering her house.
Anette's over inflated bills started in 2006. Shortly thereafter she found herself unemployed and her husband was left disabled after a car accident.
Anette Lawrence, Joburg resident
In 2010 I went back to them again, and I said to them: I cannot afford this R220 000 bill

She switched to pre-paid electricity and even though it costs more per unit, her bill dropped dramatically.
Anette
R1200, and I mean that's affordable, as opposed to what I used to get before, you know – R4000, R5000 at a shot
Billing department interior
At the same time she was put on the city's Expanded Social Package, meaning she gets her water, refuse removal and rates and taxes at a greatly reduced price. Yet she still sits with a bill of over R300 000, and, because they can't cut off her pre-paid electricity, they've cut of her water...twice...
Anette
They took out the whole unit, you know the whole meter. And all the water was gushing out. It was on a friday afternoon. They took out the whole meter, and I think by disrupting that whole meter, all the water was running into the neighbours yard, into my yard, all over the place. And everybody screaming and shouting at me. When I phoned the Joburg Water Connect it was on a weekend and they said well I have to wait until Monday. So the water was running for almost 72 hours.
Exterior shots of CoJ, laundry on a balcony etc
And yet, by law they can cut off a business's water, but a domestic household's water can only be limited. And they agree with this, even though we heard of total water cuts from a number of residents..
Stanley Maphologela Revenue and Customer relations CoJ
But for rate payers we'll only limit or restrict water supply for customers.
People at help desk
Equally strange, Yumna says queries should not take longer than a month or so to resolve, even though all our case studies have been struggling for years...
Yumna
It is not meant to take months to sort out a bill. It is not...our query resolution time is not meant to drag on indefinitely and leave customers hanging.
Exterior of Mike's building
Mike buys up derelict buildings and fixes them up.
Mike and Bon soundup:
As you can clearly see there's no such thing as a water meter here
Shots of derelict building
This building doesn't have sewerage pipes and hasn't even had any water or electricity supply for the past 8 years, and yet he still gets billed every month – at the moment the bill is standing at R14million
Mike Lingwood, Property Redeveloper
In one month we get a R278 000 account in one month for water consumption, yet there are no meters.
More shots of derelict building
Mike needs to have this sorted out before they can start fixing the building. He has followed all the right processes and escalations prescribed by the municipality – without success
Exterior shots of Swazi's building
75 year old Werner Perchtold, or Swazi, as his friends call him , owns this building in Joburg's trendy downtown Maboneng district. His problems started when they kept sending him a claimed outstanding bill from the previous owner, even though he got a clearance certificate when he took over the building.
Werner Perchtold, businessman
This is mine, and this is a company that was here ten years ago. How much do they charge them? R240 000 – maybe this one is on my account too! I don't know!
W/s Swazi and Bongani
And his own bill claims a higher consumption than is possible even if all his appliances ran 24hours per day, 7 days a week...
Swazi
In July 2011they charged me R2800, but in November they charged me R40700. I mean, then I started taking note. And, when I realised over the next 3 years, the accounts went from R900 a month, up to R26 000, August, 2013. So then I started querying it. Nobody would help me. Nobody. Just absolutely...they send me around from..City Power said it's the council, council said go to City Power.
Shots of various meters
But Yumna says that the larger bills are not neccessarily because the new smart meters are wrong – the problem was, according to her, that the old system often charged too little
Yumna
A lot of the problems that we've had so far with customers, around the smart metering, is purely a case of customers finally getting billed on actual consumption, as opposed to estimations. And these are customers who had been estimated at the lower end previously, now having to actually experience a proper reading.
Swazi with his papers
Swazi kept a meticulous record of his consumption and logged query after query, and each time when he followed it up, he was told that the query was resolved, even though nothing changed.
Swazi
So, I just decided to pay R1500 every single week, which amounts to R6000 a month.
W/s Swazi and Bongani
Now 6 years later, they still say that he owes them a small fortune..
Swazi
R343 000....
Do you have R343 000?
It's impossible. Business is so quiet. People haven't got money. And then up to 9 months ago we had load shedding every week. How can you run a business?
Ext street shot
And, like so many others he's had to keep paying bribes every time the disconnection team arrives – to be able to keep his business going...
Swazi
The people come here, they want to disconnect you, they uhm, they force you to pay a bribe, otherwise you got no power
Bongani link in street
And with the billing crisis dragging on for years now, many criminals are taking the opportunity to cash in on desperate residents
Voice over
We found an informant who agreed to speak to us on condition of anonymity
Informant
I've got a friend that works for city power, and what we do once a week is that we get an account from the city power office obviously. But mainly, we target businesses in what we call the high end areas, who have outstanding accounts. Accounts of like a couple of hundred thousand rands and stuff like that
CP workers busy with meters
Dressed up in City Power gear, they then go and cut the person off. When the upset owner confronts them, they produce the account, and negotiations start.
Informant
We do it once a week...in a bad day we can go home with two and a half thousand rand. On a good day we can go home with up to ten, fifteen thousand rand.
Yumna
Whether it's a friday night, midnight or sunday afternoon, there is someone available at the risk control dept to handle instances like this where you have people pitching up unannounced, asking for bribes, cutting off and wanting to reconnect only when a certain amount of money wants to be paid.
Swazi showing Bongani his three dud meters
To stop the account escalating further, Swazi decided to switch to pre-paid. The official at Thuso house told him that the waiting period was a year, but that she could give him a colleagues number who would help him immediately... for a small fee. Being desperate by now, he took the bait.In the end, the scamsters ripped him off three times and he ended up paying almost R20 000 in total for three meters that did not work...
Swazi and meters
Then I was informed that the prepaid meters were actually taken out in some other premises where they put a smart meter in, and they sold the prepaid meter to me...illegally
Yumna on arrests
We have had successful arrests taking place in terms of where there's collusion both from our employees side as well as our contractors. And we're asking that people come forward with information like that
Generic shots of Joburg.
But in the end, the bribery and corruption won't stop until the problems are sorted out. And, according to one of the numerous lawyers who fight city council on a full time basis, chances are that thousands of consumers who have never checked their accounts, are also paying more every month than they should be
Chantalle
Go and cheack that the meter numbers on your meters are actually the same as the one on the bill. A second thing that you could do which is quite simple – check the readings that you are being billed on, check that you are being charged the correct rates, on the correct tariff.
Traffic in street
But there may be light at the end of the tunnel
Yumna
We have a system in place, that we are working on. So that, if a customer has a problem with anything related to a meter, it doesn't matter what the problem is, the customer can basically come to a one-stop shop, more or less. And that is something that we're looking at, working on, so that we create a seamless interface for the customer, so that when they're coming through they're not send from pillar to post. We're in the process of finalising the details, the back end that needs to happen on that and we're planning to roll that out in the next few weeks
Joburg street
Although it might take a while to convince every one
Chantelle
If there are dedicated teams of people working to resolve the problem, I think they need to work harder, because the problem doesn't look like it's going away anytime soon

And, in the mean time, hordes of desperate customers are facing the same moral question every month – do I sit in the dark without water tonight, or do I keep on bribing until the miracle comes
Swazi
I don't need this aggravation, I mean i'm 75years old now. I don't want to get a heart attack and get stresed out for something twhich is not my problem.
Anette
Where do you get money, R347 00, who can just walk into the municipality and go pay R347 000. Do you know what i'm saying?




Studio outtro...
We provided the details of our case studies to City of Joburg and to City Power and they promised to look into them. In the mean time. Chantelle says, all of us would be well advised to take a monthly reading, with a photo for our own records... in case you have to go to court...




10sec Promo
A decade after the Joburg billing crisis started, the municipality claims that it's been sorted. But has it?


15sec promo nr1
What would it take to make you pay a bribe? Perhaps a R300 000 municipal bill when you feel you should be paying R3000
Upsound: Swazi – The people come here, they want to disconnect you, then they force you to pay a bribe, otherwise you've got no power


15sec promo nr2
Criminals pretending to be City Power disconnecting teams are cashing in on Joburg's billing crisis
Upsound: Informant – On a bad day we can go home with R2500.00 and on a good day we can go home with up to ten, fifteen thousand rand.

Anette Lawrence, Joburg resident In 2010 I went back to them again, and I said to them: I cannot afford this R220 000 bill She switched to pre-paid electricity and even though it costs more per unit, her bill dropped dramatically. Anette R1200, and I mean that's affordable, as opposed to what I used to get before, you know – R4000, R5000 at a shot Billing department interior At the same time she was put on the city's Expanded Social Package, meaning she gets her water, refuse removal and rates and taxes at a greatly reduced price. Yet she still sits with a bill of over R300 000, and, because they can't cut off her pre-paid electricity, they've cut of her water...twice... Anette They took out the whole unit, you know the whole meter. And all the water was gushing out. It was on a friday afternoon. They took out the whole meter, and I think by disrupting that whole meter, all the water was running into the neighbours yard, into my yard, all over the place. And everybody screaming and shouting at me. When I phoned the Joburg Water Connect it was on a weekend and they said well I have to wait until Monday. So the water was running for almost 72 hours. Exterior shots of CoJ, laundry on a balcony etc And yet, by law they can cut off a business's water, but a domestic household's water can only be limited. And they agree with this, even though we heard of total water cuts from a number of residents.. Stanley Maphologela Revenue and Customer relations CoJ But for rate payers we'll only limit or restrict water supply for customers. People at help desk Equally strange, Yumna says queries should not take longer than a month or so to resolve, even though all our case studies have been struggling for years... Yumna It is not meant to take months to sort out a bill. It is not...our query resolution time is not meant to drag on indefinitely and leave customers hanging. Exterior of Mike's building Mike buys up derelict buildings and fixes them up. Mike and Bon soundup: As you can clearly see there's no such thing as a water meter here Shots of derelict building This building doesn't have sewerage pipes and hasn't even had any water or electricity supply for the past 8 years, and yet he still gets billed every month – at the moment the bill is standing at R14million Mike Lingwood, Property Redeveloper In one month we get a R278 000 account in one month for water consumption, yet there are no meters. More shots of derelict building Mike needs to have this sorted out before they can start fixing the building. He has followed all the right processes and escalations prescribed by the municipality – without success Exterior shots of Swazi's building 75 year old Werner Perchtold, or Swazi, as his friends call him , owns this building in Joburg's trendy downtown Maboneng district. His problems started when they kept sending him a claimed outstanding bill from the previous owner, even though he got a clearance certificate when he took over the building. Werner Perchtold, businessman This is mine, and this is a company that was here ten years ago. How much do they charge them? R240 000 – maybe this one is on my account too! I don't know! W/s Swazi and Bongani And his own bill claims a higher consumption than is possible even if all his appliances ran 24hours per day, 7 days a week... Swazi In July 2011they charged me R2800, but in November they charged me R40700. I mean, then I started taking note. And, when I realised over the next 3 years, the accounts went from R900 a month, up to R26 000, August, 2013. So then I started querying it. Nobody would help me. Nobody. Just absolutely...they send me around from..City Power said it's the council, council said go to City Power. Shots of various meters But Yumna says that the larger bills are not neccessarily because the new smart meters are wrong – the problem was, according to her, that the old system often charged too little Yumna A lot of the problems that we've had so far with customers, around the smart metering, is purely a case of customers finally getting billed on actual consumption, as opposed to estimations. And these are customers who had been estimated at the lower end previously, now having to actually experience a proper reading. Swazi with his papers Swazi kept a meticulous record of his consumption and logged query after query, and each time when he followed it up, he was told that the query was resolved, even though nothing changed. Swazi So, I just decided to pay R1500 every single week, which amounts to R6000 a month. W/s Swazi and Bongani Now 6 years later, they still say that he owes them a small fortune.. Swazi R343 000.... Do you have R343 000? It's impossible. Business is so quiet. People haven't got money. And then up to 9 months ago we had load shedding every week. How can you run a business? Ext street shot And, like so many others he's had to keep paying bribes every time the disconnection team arrives – to be able to keep his business going... Swazi The people come here, they want to disconnect you, they uhm, they force you to pay a bribe, otherwise you got no power Bongani link in street And with the billing crisis dragging on for years now, many criminals are taking the opportunity to cash in on desperate residents Voice over We found an informant who agreed to speak to us on condition of anonymity Informant I've got a friend that works for city power, and what we do once a week is that we get an account from the city power office obviously. But mainly, we target businesses in what we call the high end areas, who have outstanding accounts. Accounts of like a couple of hundred thousand rands and stuff like that CP workers busy with meters Dressed up in City Power gear, they then go and cut the person off. When the upset owner confronts them, they produce the account, and negotiations start. Informant We do it once a week...in a bad day we can go home with two and a half thousand rand. On a good day we can go home with up to ten, fifteen thousand rand. Yumna Whether it's a friday night, midnight or sunday afternoon, there is someone available at the risk control dept to handle instances like this where you have people pitching up unannounced, asking for bribes, cutting off and wanting to reconnect only when a certain amount of money wants to be paid. Swazi showing Bongani his three dud meters To stop the account escalating further, Swazi decided to switch to pre-paid. The official at Thuso house told him that the waiting period was a year, but that she could give him a colleagues number who would help him immediately... for a small fee. Being desperate by now, he took the bait.In the end, the scamsters ripped him off three times and he ended up paying almost R20 000 in total for three meters that did not work... Swazi and meters Then I was informed that the prepaid meters were actually taken out in some other premises where they put a smart meter in, and they sold the prepaid meter to me...illegally Yumna on arrests We have had successful arrests taking place in terms of where there's collusion both from our employees side as well as our contractors. And we're asking that people come forward with information like that Generic shots of Joburg. But in the end, the bribery and corruption won't stop until the problems are sorted out. And, according to one of the numerous lawyers who fight city council on a full time basis, chances are that thousands of consumers who have never checked their accounts, are also paying more every month than they should be Chantalle Go and cheack that the meter numbers on your meters are actually the same as the one on the bill. A second thing that you could do which is quite simple – check the readings that you are being billed on, check that you are being charged the correct rates, on the correct tariff. Traffic in street But there may be light at the end of the tunnel Yumna We have a system in place, that we are working on. So that, if a customer has a problem with anything related to a meter, it doesn't matter what the problem is, the customer can basically come to a one-stop shop, more or less. And that is something that we're looking at, working on, so that we create a seamless interface for the customer, so that when they're coming through they're not send from pillar to post. We're in the process of finalising the details, the back end that needs to happen on that and we're planning to roll that out in the next few weeks Joburg street Although it might take a while to convince every one Chantelle If there are dedicated teams of people working to resolve the problem, I think they need to work harder, because the problem doesn't look like it's going away anytime soon And, in the mean time, hordes of desperate customers are facing the same moral question every month – do I sit in the dark without water tonight, or do I keep on bribing until the miracle comes Swazi I don't need this aggravation, I mean i'm 75years old now. I don't want to get a heart attack and get stresed out for something twhich is not my problem. Anette Where do you get money, R347 00, who can just walk into the municipality and go pay R347 000. Do you know what i'm saying? Studio outtro... We provided the details of our case studies to City of Joburg and to City Power and they promised to look into them. In the mean time. Chantelle says, all of us would be well advised to take a monthly reading, with a photo for our own records... in case you have to go to court... 10sec Promo A decade after the Joburg billing crisis started, the municipality claims that it's been sorted. But has it? 15sec promo nr1 What would it take to make you pay a bribe? Perhaps a R300 000 municipal bill when you feel you should be paying R3000 Upsound: Swazi – The people come here, they want to disconnect you, then they force you to pay a bribe, otherwise you've got no power 15sec promo nr2 Criminals pretending to be City Power disconnecting teams are cashing in on Joburg's billing crisis Upsound: Informant – On a bad day we can go home with R2500.00 and on a good day we can go home with up to ten, fifteen thousand rand.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): If you are living in jozi, chances are that you are being billed a lot more for your electricity than you are actually using
metadata.Summary: Ten years after they first admitted that they had billing problems, City Power recently went on record to say that it has been solved. But this is a lie - according to various legal firms, the Star Consumer Watch, and thousands of consumers. Wrong meter numbers, meters that are only ever estimated and never actually read and adjusted, and impossible consumption figures have lead to a chaos that is not about to be solved soon - and which is costing consumers millions of rands, and which leads to power and (illegal) water cuts by the council. Council has an approach of first pay the amount showing on your bill and then we will investigate your claim that it's wrong. This leads to the start of corruption from honest citizens - people who come to disconnect are simply bribed not to cut the power or water. At the same time this has also lead to various scams appearing - people who either work for city power or act as if they do, arrive at your gate and threaten to disconnect you unless you pay a bribe. We even have a case study of a guy who was phoned by someone from city power and told that they were mailing him his account and he had to pay R35 000 to bring it up to date - he received the account via email, paid the money and then realised a few days later that he was scammed. He went to City Power, phoned the guy's number from another official's desk, and they heard the phone ring in an empty cubicle down the passage. According to one lawyer we interviewed, the matter should really be taken to concourt - as an old bylaw seems to lie at the heart of the problem - this states that the burden of proof in cases against the municipality lies with the consumer - meaning that we all have to do our own daily readings with photographs. In spite of this, they have a whole dapertment dealing with these cases only, and in 8 years have only lost three cases.
